facts.text: Spokane began as Spokane Plantation, a cotton plantation established in Concordia Parish during the antebellum era along the Mississippi River delta.
The Conner family, originally from South Carolina, moved into Louisiana in the 1840s and bought Spokane to exploit the fertile alluvial soils for cotton.
Spokane sits on the southwestern shore of Lake St., a 2,200‑acre oxbow lake formed by a former Mississippi River meander.
The community lies about four miles west of the Mississippi River, where silt‑laden soils support cotton and soybean farming.
During the 1850s, Spokane’s cotton production relied on a network of brokerage firms in New Orleans and levee maintenance to curb flooding.
The area’s humid subtropical climate brings long, hot summers with highs often above 92°F and mild winters averaging around 39°F.
